changelog:
STILL ON VERSION 1.6.6? If Install says "App not installed", do this once (we changed the app's security key):
1. Make sure you have the Downloader app (Main Apps, Amazon Appstore or Google Play).
2. Uninstall Snow Media Center: Main Apps > Snow Media Center > Uninstall, or Settings > Applications > Snow Media Center > Uninstall.
3. Open Downloader, enter code 9073972 and install.
4. Open Snow Media Center and sign in once. Updates install normally again after this.

WHAT'S NEW
Voice commands: press the mic next to Settings on the home screen (or the Search button on your remote) and just say it: "put on ESPN", "watch The Office", "open YouTube", "take me to the Guide", "search for Batman". Anything else goes to the Snow Media AI, which answers or takes you there. Kids profiles keep their limits.
Profiles: "Who's watching?" when the app opens. Everyone in the house gets their own profile with its own Continue Watching, My List, Live TV favourites and home screen, and it follows your Snow Media account to any box. Kids profiles only show Plex titles up to the age you pick and the kids and family channels in Live TV, with no Store, Games or Settings. Add a 4-digit PIN to any profile; forgot it? After a few tries, Forgot PIN emails you a reset code and lets our support team know. Settings > UI > Profiles.
Plex My List: press My List on any movie or show to save it; your list is a row on Plex Home and follows your Snow Media account to any box.
Plex remembers where YOU stopped: Continue Watching, Resume and the progress bars are now your own, not everyone's, and they follow your Snow Media account to any box you sign in on.
Plex shows: Skip Intro appears during a show's intro, and at the end credits an Up Next card counts down and plays the next episode (OK plays it now, Back keeps watching the credits). It carries on into the next season too.
Plex is faster on every box: posters come down at the size they are drawn, libraries no longer download your whole collection in the background, moving through the menu and rails no longer reloads what you pass, and older boxes get the lighter layout automatically.
Plex keeps your place: closing a movie or episode puts you back exactly where you were (the same rail, the same episode list), each rail remembers where you left it, and holding OK no longer opens a title and then plays it.
Plex settles before it shows: a short "Getting Plex ready…" while every Home rail and its posters load, so the screen is smooth the moment it appears instead of stuttering while rows arrive behind the remote. Capped at nine seconds.
Plex search: before you type, a row of Popular searches (what everyone has been looking for) and your Recent searches on this box. Down from the search box lands on them, OK searches.
Plex search forgives typos: a missing apostrophe, colon or letter no longer means no results — a "Did you mean" row offers the closest titles, and OK opens one.
Plex Home: Recently Added and Recently Released go a hundred titles deep, and the rails only draw the tiles near the highlight, so scrolling them is smooth on any box.
Live TV: a VOD section is back in the menu with your line's movies, and Plex pinned first — OK takes you straight into Plex, and Back brings you back to VOD. Live TV now opens with the highlight on the categories.
Live TV is lighter: programme info only loads for the channels on screen, categories load when you stop on one instead of for every one you pass, channel lists are let go when you leave, and radio channels no longer restart every few seconds.
Remote media buttons work in the Player: Play/Pause pauses and resumes Live TV, Plex, VOD and Backups; Fast-forward and Rewind skip 30 s ahead / 10 s back in films and episodes, and change channel in Live TV.
Multi-Screen: the channel picker is a big, readable panel, and Back from a full-screen tile returns to your screens instead of the layout chooser.
Live TV and VOD: the category list scrolls with the highlight all the way down. The Grid layout is now called Vibez and no longer plays a hidden preview.
The Player signs itself in with your billing or Snow Media account when this box has no login saved (the sign-in form shows if it can't).
Guide: a preview window plays the highlighted channel with what's on now and next, and Back from a channel returns to the same spot in the Guide.
Plex search: can't find it? A "Not on Plex yet? Request it" row shows what we can add; press OK on one to see it and request it (movies, and shows with every season). It's usually on Plex within a few hours, and this box gets a notification when it's ready — even with the app closed.
Plex search: popular and recent searches show as posters in rows you can move through with Up and Down, and results always show their cover art.
Player Settings → Appearance scrolls with the highlight down to Background and Text color, and shows a picture of each Live TV layout. Pick one and Live TV opens in it; a few seconds later it asks Keep or Change.
Opening the old Dreamstreams, VibezTV or Plex app now suggests the Player, with what it adds; Continue opens the app as before, and "Don't show this again" turns the suggestion off.
Buffering guide redesigned: bigger text you can read from the couch, a step tracker across the top, large answer buttons, the main button first on every step, and your results with Send to support right at the top.
Main Apps: Dreamstreams, VibezTV and Plex now point you to the Player. They live under Live TV and Plex there; Open Player takes you straight to the right section.
Plex Halloween: from late September a Halloween entry sits at the top of your Plex libraries — a hand-picked collection split into Kids & Family, Family Spooky Shows, Halloween Night, Occult & Possession, Haunted Houses & Ghosts, Slashers, Vampires & Monsters, Zombies, Horror Comedies, Psychological Horror and Spooky Series, showing what is on your server.
Plex buffering card says why: it knows what the video needs, so it tells you whether your internet is too slow for it, the Plex server can't send it fast enough, or the Plex Relay is limiting it — and which quality to pick.

FIXES
Older Android boxes (X96, T95): the Dashboard and Settings buttons sit at the top right again instead of over the logo.
Plex: the side menu and the content start below the TV's overscan band, so the server line is no longer cut off at the top. Left from the search box goes back to the menu.
Device Cleaner: the button titles are white again instead of dark grey on blue.
Plex quality: switching to 1080p · 8 Mbps (or any lower quality) no longer gives up after a few seconds and falls back to the original; the server gets time to start converting.
Plex buffers less: films still start at their original quality, and if one keeps buffering because it needs more than your connection or the server gives, the Player drops to a quality that fits (like the Plex app does) and tells you. The Player also keeps Wi-Fi at full speed while a video plays and keeps more of the film loaded ahead on 2 GB boxes.

Plus everything in 1.7.6: Plex opens lighter and kinder to small boxes, and nothing adult on the content bar or the Plex Home, Discover and Search rails.
releaseNotes: Still on 1.6.6 and the update says "App not installed"? Uninstall Snow Media Center once, then reinstall it with Downloader code 9073972. Version 1.7.7 adds profiles for everyone in the house (Kids profiles and optional PINs included) and voice commands, makes Plex faster on every box (tile-sized posters, no home-screen chores under the rails), settles Plex before it appears, forgives typos in Plex search with a Did-you-mean row, adds popular and recent searches, brings VOD back to Live TV with Plex pinned first, makes Live TV lighter on memory, deepens the Home rails to a hundred titles, points Dreamstreams, VibezTV and Plex in Main Apps to the Player, and fixes the header on older Android boxes. Installs normally over 1.7.6.
